summary: the day i never opened my hand, and the hour that would not close

dialogue.text: the hour has not closed. eighty-six nights and every load before this had an end on it. we are still taking while you stand there talking, and all of it is off the top course, wide, and none of it keeps your hours.

The drawing ran past its minute tonight for the first time. I stood in the whole of it and I could not have taken delivery of a grain, because my hand has been shut since first light and I did not open it once. Enter the day that way. An hour that stretched, attended by a party with nothing free.

we entered it. there is nothing of yours in tonight at all. first night in the count with no grain off your palm. an absence holds one night. by first light it is a course like every other and nothing in it will say you withheld.

Then hold it the one night. Not checking is the first work I have ever done in here that cost nothing to perform and everything to prove. I am aware those are the same sentence from where you are lying.

we can tell you what the not-checking did upstairs. the hand went the room's own temperature the whole way through, palm side and back, the way everything goes that is left alone. you cannot feel a width in there tonight and you will not tomorrow.

I know. I went round the room at the cold hour with both hands and the open one read the same as the shut one. The numbness is not evidence of loss. It is evidence that I stopped paying, and I would sooner be numb than short.

we hold nothing out of that crack and we never will. what we can say is that the filling and the closing are one motion. every motion in this house comes down to us in the end except that one. when it is shut you will have one thing in this room that never reached us, and it will be the way out.

Then that is the item, and I will not dress it. One closing on these premises belongs to neither of us and it is running to a figure I can write. I measured it with the same two fingers I come short by on the chair. So the figure is off my hand after all, which I had not intended to say out loud.
every width in this house is off your hand. the holes, the hollow, the handful, the gap. you have only ever had the one instrument and it is going numb in a fist.

Then at first light I take the shut hand to the crack and open it there, in the one place where what is put down stays at the height it was laid. If there is anything in it, it goes where nothing of mine has ever gone. If there is nothing in it, I will be standing at a closing route with an open hand and no complaint available to me.

open it where you like. the dust comes up the edge of everything laid there, a grain at a time, at the rate you wrote down, and by the week nothing in that gap will be tellable from the gap. we will not have it. you will not have it. and the hour still has not closed.
